scope: Proposition 8.2 (Microscopic smallness) of the manuscript “BKT universality for height and planar spin fields” (preprints/BKT-universality-for-height-and-planar-spin-fields-September-24-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 216 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 5e6a8df09e021c4a), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 124. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: For a′ in a fixed compact interval containing k0 or lying above it, the two ultraviolet integrations have the exact block representation K0(X) = 1X={B}{se0 B/2 + z0cα B} + R0(X), z0 = 2m2 0e−a′Duv/2 . (8.11) For spread-out Jρ, choose 1/2 < γ′ < γ and put δ0 = e−γ′a′v2/2. For exponentially small s, ∥R0∥ ≤ CρC (|s| + δ0)2 , ∥∂sR0∥ ≤ CρC (|s| + δ0). (8.12) Thus, uniformly on |s| ≤ C′z0, these bounds are o(z0) and o(1), respectively. Uniformly towards unbounded a′, it suffices to use the weaker bounds CρC(s2+δ0) and CρC(|s|+δ0), and the designated cosine may be absorbed in the remainder. For fixed J these weaker bounds hold with CJ and any fixed 0 < γ′ < γ when a′ is sufficiently large.
